anomalies.obs: On the EPD_Driver sheet the FPC connector J2 carries the same global net labels on two separate pins: pin2 and pin14 both = NET0012, pin3 and pin13 both = NET0032, pin4 and pin12 both = NET0006. Pin2 is wired to the boost MOSFET Q2 gate (GDR) and pin3 to R3 (RESE), while pins 12/13/14 are the CSB/SCL/SDA lines that run to the SKW92A on the SkylabModule sheet.
anomalies.exp: Per the specification the GDR/RESE nodes belong only to the panel's internal boost loop ("Q1's gate ... driven from J1.2 ... R1 ... to J1.3 (RESE) ... the SKW92A only issues SPI commands ... it does not directly control the boost converter's switching"), and the SPI lines (J1.12-14) are distinct nets to the module. Pins 2/3/4 must not share nets with pins 12/13/14.

evidence.quote: EPD_Driver.kicad_sch: J2 pin2 and pin14 both labelled NET0012; pin3 and pin13 both NET0032; pin4 and pin12 both NET0006; Q2 gate wire to pin2, R3 to pin3

Q1's gate ... is driven from J1.2 — the EPD panel's own GDR pin ... Q1's source ... returns through R1 ... to J1.3 (RESE) ... the SKW92A only issues SPI commands and toggles the Q2 power-switch GPIO; it does not directly control the boost converter's switching.

anomalies.impact: The high-voltage boost switching node (GDR) and the current-sense node (RESE) are shorted to the SPI clock/data/chip-select lines that connect to the SKW92A GPIOs. This corrupts the EPD SPI interface, breaks the boost control loop, and exposes the module's I/O pins to the boosted panel voltage, likely damaging the GPIOs. The display would not function.

parsed.summary: The EPD FPC connector J2 has duplicate global net labels tying the boost-converter GDR/RESE pins (2,3) and pin 4 to the SPI control pins (14,13,12), merging the high-voltage switching/sense nodes with the module's SPI lines — a bridged-nets deviation from the reference design.
